script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

Title: "The Great Unknown"

INT. GYM - DAY

A small-town gym bustles with activity. PEOPLE of all ages and shapes work out on various equipment. A TRainer, JIM, yells encouraging words to a CLIENT, SARA, as she lifts a weight.

JIM
(shouting)
Just a few more reps, Sara! You've got this!

SARA
(grunting)
I'm trying, Jim!

The door bursts open, and in walks a STRANGER, COLE. He's in his late 20s, dressed in athletic clothing, and carrying a large backpack. He takes a moment to take in the scene, then approaches the reception desk.

RECEPTIONIST
(cheerful)
Welcome to our gym, sir! How can I help you today?

COLE
(leaning on the counter)
I'm looking for a place to train for the upcoming regional track meet. I heard this was a good gym.

RECEPTIONIST
(smiling)
You made a great choice! We have some of the best trainers in the region. Let me introduce you to Jim.

Jim looks up from his client, intrigued.

INT. GYM - TRAINING ROOM - LATER

Jim and Cole are now in the training room, going over Cole's training schedule.

JIM
(skeptical)
Regional track meet? Which events are you competing in?

COLE
(determined)
The 400-meter dash and the long jump. I've been training on my own for months, but I need to take my game to the next level.

Jim nods, impressed.

JIM
I'll do my best to help you out. Let's get started.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jim and Cole sit in a cozy corner booth, sipping coffee and discussing Cole's training regimen.

COLE
(earnest)
I really want to make it to the national championships. It's a long shot, I know, but I believe I have what it takes.

JIM
(sympathetic)
Belief is a powerful thing, Cole. But you need more than that to make it to the top. You need dedication, hard work, and a little bit of luck.

COLE
(nodding)
I'm ready for that.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL TRACK - DAY

Cole and Jim are now at the high school track, where Cole trains with a group of local athletes. Cole runs laps, does drills, and practices his long jumps, with Jim coaching him every step of the way.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - NIGHT

Jim and Cole sit in the same booth, exhausted from their training session. They talk about Cole's progress and his dreams of making it to the national championships.

COLE
(determined)
I'm going to make it happen, Jim. I just know it.

JIM
(smiling)
I believe you, Cole. Keep working hard.

INT. GYM - DAY

Months have passed, and Cole is now a regular at the gym. He's noticeably stronger and faster, and the other athletes look up to him. Jim watches proudly as Cole runs on the treadmill, pushing himself to the limit.

INT. REGIONAL TRACK MEET - DAY

Cole competes in the 400-meter dash and the long jump, and he performs exceptionally well in both events. The crowd goes wild as he crosses the finish line and soars through the air in the long jump pit.

INT. NATIONAL TRACK STADIUM - DAY

Cole is now at the national championships, and the stakes are higher than ever. He's nervous, but he's determined to give it his all. Jim is there to support him, along with the entire town, which has rallied behind him.

COLE
(to himself)
I can do this.

INT. NATIONAL TRACK STADIUM - FINALS - NIGHT

The finals are here, and Cole is up against the best athletes in the country. He runs the 400-meter dash with all his might, and he soars through the air in the long jump pit, setting a new record.

The crowd goes wild as Cole stands on the podium, receiving his medal.

ANNOUNCER (V.O.)
Ladies and gentlemen, we have a new national champion!

Cole looks up to the sky, a smile on his face, and dedicates his victory to his small town and to Jim, who believed in him when no one else did.

INT. GYM - DAY

Jim watches Cole's victory on the TV, surrounded by the townspeople who have come to the gym to celebrate.

JIM
(voice shaking with emotion)
I'm so proud of you, Cole. You've shown us all that with hard work and determination, anything is possible.

FADE OUT.

THE END
